newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end firmer, outperform as dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end firmer, outperform as dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, outperforming U.S. Treasuries, amid a stronger currency and renewed investor interest in Canada's positive bond market fundamentals, analysts said.

"The Beige Book report seemed to raise a bit of concern about wage pressures in the U.S. economy. Those are not really concerns here in Canada. The Canadian dollar did very well," said Ted Carmichael, head of research with J.P. Morgan Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.20 to C$110.90 to yield 7.083 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 7/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 38 basis points from 45 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
"People seem comfortable getting back into Canada. There was some pretty good foreign interest today," said one Toronto-based bond trader.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets initially rallied this morning after the U.S. government reported that the U.S. gross domestic product grew by 2.2 percent in the third quarter. But U.S. bonds later pared gains on Beige Book wage pressure worries.

Analysts said Canadian bonds are once again benefitting from the country's positive bond market fundamentals, which include a weak economy, declining government deficits, low interest rates and inflation well below that of the United States.
Canada's positive fundamentals last week brought longer-term Canada-U.S. bond spreads to their lowest levels since 1985.
Canadian bonds also benefitted from strength in the Canadian dollar, which was boosted by a bullish report on the Canadian currency from Goldman Sachs, dealers said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.10 to C$103.90 to yield 6.466 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 5/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from 12 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.18 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.14 percent.
